outcome: complications (disseminated intravascular coagulation, intestinal obstruction, acute renal failure, vesicovaginal fistula)
cohort: The study included seven women who underwent damage control surgery for near-miss maternal mortality due to placenta previa and/or placenta accreta spectrum at King Abdulaziz University Hospital, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, between November 1, 2007, and March 1, 2020.
finding: Damage control surgery was found to be a life-saving intervention for women experiencing near-miss mortality due to obstetrical hemorrhage associated with placenta previa and/or placenta accreta spectrum.
